Lemon Squeezy migration inventory checklist

Before choosing or configuring a replacement payment provider, map every place where Lemon Squeezy touches your product. This standalone checklist works without buying a tool.

Published November 22, 2026 · by the maker of LS Exit Audit

Scope: inventory only. Do not move customer records, subscriptions, licenses, payments, or credentials during this step. Scan only repositories and URLs you own or are authorized to assess.

1. Create one inventory record per dependency

Use these fields so each finding has an owner and a verifiable exit condition:

Location | Dependency | Current behavior | Migration owner | Replacement | Verification step | Status ---------|------------|------------------|-----------------|-------------|-------------------|------- app/api/webhook.ts | subscription webhook | updates access state | Backend | TBD | replay sanitized fixture | Open

2. Repository and configuration

  • SDK imports, package dependencies, API clients, and generated types
  • Environment-variable names, secret references, and deployment configuration — record names, never secret values
  • Store, product, variant, subscription, order, and customer identifiers
  • Checkout URL builders, pricing buttons, overlays, and return URLs
  • Customer-portal links and account-management actions
  • Webhook endpoints, signature verification, event names, retries, and idempotency logic
  • Subscription status mapping, cancellation, pause, refund, grace-period, and failed-payment behavior
  • License activation, validation, deactivation, device limits, and offline fallback
  • Tests, fixtures, mocks, seed data, CI variables, deployment scripts, and monitoring queries
  • Comments, runbooks, onboarding docs, privacy text, terms, agent instructions, and support macros

3. Customer-facing web surface

  • Pricing pages, plan comparison tables, checkout buttons, and embedded storefronts
  • Help center, billing FAQ, cancellation instructions, and refund policy
  • Login, account, download, license, and purchase-confirmation pages
  • Email templates for receipts, renewals, failed payments, cancellations, and license delivery
  • Affiliate links, campaign pages, partner pages, and public documentation
  • Terms, privacy policy, data-processing disclosures, invoices, and tax wording
  • Browser extensions, desktop-app update flows, plugins, mobile apps, and external installers

4. Operational gaps to assign explicitly

  • Existing subscriptions: migration, parallel operation, customer reauthorization, or controlled wind-down
  • PayPal and alternative-payment customers that the replacement may not support
  • License keys, file delivery, download entitlements, storefront pages, and affiliate management
  • Webhook ordering, duplicate delivery, missing events, and access removal after expiry
  • Refunds, disputes, invoices, taxes, historical exports, and support access after cutover
  • Unsupported seller countries, currencies, payout rails, or business types
  • Rollback owner, freeze window, monitoring dashboard, and customer escalation route

5. Verification before cutover

  • Search again for old domains, SDK names, environment variables, IDs, and brand text
  • Test new checkout, webhook, portal, refund, cancellation, renewal, and failed-payment paths
  • Test access removal and license behavior, not only successful purchase
  • Review every public page and customer email on desktop and mobile
  • Keep a documented rollback path until production evidence is stable
  • Archive the final inventory with owners, evidence links, and unresolved exceptions

Official planning references

Confirm deadlines and provider-specific limitations directly in Lemon Squeezy's current migration guide, migration FAQ, and comparison guidance. Policies can change; use the official pages as the source of truth.
